newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Navy says China rehearsed Taiwan invasion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy says China rehearsed Taiwan invasion.

text.p: China was rehearsing for a possible future all-out invasion of Taiwan during war games that overshadowed the island's first democratic presidential vote in March, the U.S. Navy's intelligence office concluded in a study made available on Monday.
The Office of Naval Intelligence, or ONI, interpreted the March 8 to 25 exercises as a series of rehearsals for an invasion as well as an attempt by Beijing to cow the island's voters.

"This was the latest and largest in what ONI assesses to be a series of rehearsals of a contingency scenario for the invasion of Taiwan" that was first identified by the Navy in its analysis of a 1994 command post exercise, the study said.
Key parts of the Navy's May 1996 intelligence study were made available to Reuters by Defense Week, which published an article based on it in an issue out on Tuesday.

Codenamed Strait 961, the operation appears to have been China's largest multi-service exercise in the Taiwan Strait, even though bad weather interfered with its final phase, the analysis said. Carried out in three separately announced rounds, it involved missile tests to target areas less than 35 miles (55 km) from Taiwan and combined force operations.

In reaction to the live-fire military tests, the United States sent two aircraft carrier battle groups to the waters around Taiwan. The presence of the battle groups, condemned by China, marked the largest U.S. buildup in the area since the Vietnam War ended with a Communist victory in 1975.

Rather than being a series of distinct exercises, as Beijing's announcement of "new exercises" on March 9 and March 15 could be interpreted to suggest, the war games appeared to be part of a unified invasion plan, the study suggested.

"It can be surmised that China sought to gauge its progress in being able to carry out, in a joint warfighting environment, the contingency Taiwan invasion scenario first played out in the 1994 Command Post exercise," it said.

But it concurred with other Pentagon findings that China's People's Liberation Army currently was ill-prepared to invade Taiwan successfully. China regards Taiwan as a renegade province because it was a refuge for Nationalist troops who lost their civil war to the communists in 1949.

Logistics and amphibious lift capability must be improved before Beijing can mount a "real-world" invasion, the study said. "Also, we do not believe the Chinese have the logisitics capability to support the operations of a large complement of forward deployed forces conducting high intensity warfare."

An administration official who monitors China voiced surprise at the Navy conclusion that Beijing had been rehearsing for a possible future invasion, although he acknowledged the war games' training component.
"But that's a long way from full-scale rehearsal of an all-out invasion plan," said the official who asked not to be named. The Navy had no immediate comment on the study.
